reasons: The lake record is verified and identifies the case as United States v. Ross, decided by the U.S. Supreme Court on 1982-06-01, with year 1982.
The lake official citation is 456 U.S. 798; the listed parallel citations and vendor-neutral citation match the assertion.

Ross directly defines the scope of the automobile exception: the opinion states that the Carroll exception permits a warrantless vehicle search no broader and no narrower than a magistrate could authorize by warrant.
The opinion frames the case as deciding what police may search when they have probable cause to believe contraband is concealed somewhere within a lawfully stopped automobile.
The opinion squarely addresses whether officers conducting a lawful warrantless automobile search may open containers found within the vehicle.
The text supports the container bridge role by stating that the search scope is not defined by container type, but by the object sought and places where probable cause supports finding it.

defect.evidence_quote: If probable cause justifies the search of a lawfully stopped vehicle, it justifies the search of every part of the vehicle and its contents that may conceal the object of the search.
defect.problem: The holding summary is overbroad as written because it says probable cause justifies searching every container, but Ross limits the search to vehicle contents that may conceal the object of the search.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise the holding to: When PC justifies the search of a lawfully stopped vehicle, it justifies the search of every part of the vehicle and its contents that may conceal the object of the search.

reasons: The exact holding contains the limiting phrase 'that may conceal the object of the search.'
The page-824 rule also limits scope by the object of the search and the places where there is probable cause to believe it may be found.
residual_risks: The ellipsis may have been intended as shorthand, but the displayed holding omits the operative limiting language.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the exact Ross formulation: every part of the vehicle and its contents that may conceal the object of the search.
